1001.principle: Use generative AI when the deliverable is new content (text, image, code, summary); use predictive ML when the deliverable is a score, label, or forecast.
1001.principle_hinglish: Agar output naya content hai (text, image) to gen AI; agar number ya forecast chahiye to predictive ML.

1002.principle: AI > machine learning > deep learning > generative AI: each is a narrower technique inside the previous one.
1002.principle_hinglish: AI sabse bada, uske andar ML, phir deep learning, aur gen AI naya content banane wala hissa.

1003.principle: Do not default to generative AI: scoring and classification with labeled history is usually best served by predictive ML, with gen AI complementing it.
1003.principle_hinglish: Fraud scoring jaise labeled-data tasks ke liye predictive ML pehle dekho; gen AI summary jaise kaam me madad karta hai.

1004.principle: Summarisation and classification of unstructured text are everyday generative language capabilities.
1004.principle_hinglish: Lambe free-text ko chhota karke themes nikalna gen AI ki summarisation capability hai.

1005.principle: Early wins pair repetitive drafting or summarising work with human review; avoid autonomous high-stakes decisions.
1005.principle_hinglish: Shuruaati projects me drafting + insaan ka review rakho; high-risk faisle model par mat chhodo.

1006.principle: Ask what technique the product uses and which business task it performs; 'AI' alone is not a specification.
1006.principle_hinglish: 'AI-powered' sirf label hai; technique aur kaam poochho.

1007.principle: Generative AI speeds drafting but does not certify correctness; keep accountable human review where claims carry legal weight.
1007.principle_hinglish: Gen AI draft jaldi deta hai, compliance ki guarantee nahi; review zaroori hai.

1008.principle: Pick the technique that fits the task, then rank projects by value, data readiness and team capacity.
1008.principle_hinglish: Kaam ke hisaab se technique chuno, phir value aur readiness se priority.

1009.principle: Generative models excel at creating and transforming content; they do not by themselves verify truth or replace qualified review.
1009.principle_hinglish: Gen AI content banata aur badalta hai; sach verify nahi karta.

1010.principle: Multimodal models handle combinations of text, images, audio and video in one workflow.
1010.principle_hinglish: Multimodal model photo aur text dono ek saath samajh sakta hai.

1011.principle: When an assistant plans and acts across systems with tools, it is behaving as an agent and needs permission and oversight design.
1011.principle_hinglish: Jab assistant tools use karke multi-step kaam karta hai, wo agent hai; permission aur nigrani chahiye.

1012.principle: Start with bounded, internal, human-reviewed tasks where value can be measured and risk is limited.
1012.principle_hinglish: Pilot chhota, internal aur review-wala rakho.

1013.principle: Judge gen AI pilots on outcomes against a baseline (time, quality, cost, revenue), not on usage or enthusiasm.
1013.principle_hinglish: Value baseline ke saath naapo: time, quality, win rate; sirf usage nahi.

1014.principle: Start from business problems and readiness, not from competitor announcements.
1014.principle_hinglish: Competition ke dabav me nahi, business problem se shuru karo.

1015.principle: Use gen AI for drafts and summaries that a professional verifies; keep authoritative judgment and records with accountable people and systems.
1015.principle_hinglish: Draft aur summary ke liye gen AI; final kanooni faisla vakil ka.

1016.principle: A foundation model is broadly pre-trained and adaptable, so one model can serve many tasks through prompting, grounding or tuning.
1016.principle_hinglish: Foundation model bade data par pehle se train hota hai, isliye kai kaam kar sakta hai.

1017.principle: Tokens are the units of text a model reads and writes; they drive cost, latency and context limits.
1017.principle_hinglish: Token matlab text ke tukde; zyada token = zyada cost aur time.

1018.principle: The context window bounds how much input a model can consider; long content calls for chunking, retrieval or larger windows.
1018.principle_hinglish: Context window = model ek baar me kitna input dekh sakta hai.

1019.principle: An LLM learns language patterns from large text corpora and generates likely continuations; fluency does not guarantee accuracy.
1019.principle_hinglish: LLM text ke patterns seekhta hai aur agla likha hua predict karta hai.

1020.principle: Match model modality to the inputs and outputs of the workflow.
1020.principle_hinglish: Input me photo/audio ho to multimodal model chuno.

1021.principle: Generative output is probabilistic; some variation is normal and can be reduced with settings, structure and evaluation.
1021.principle_hinglish: Gen AI probability se likhta hai, isliye har baar thoda alag jawab aa sakta hai.

1022.principle: Open models give control and inspectability at the price of added responsibility; fit depends on requirements, not a blanket preference.
1022.principle_hinglish: Open model me control zyada, lekin zimmedari bhi zyada.

1023.principle: Choose models by the modality of the required output as well as the input.
1023.principle_hinglish: Output video chahiye to video generate karne wala model chuno.

1024.principle: Models learn mostly in training; to use company knowledge you supply it at request time or adapt the model deliberately.
1024.principle_hinglish: Chat se model permanent nahi seekhta; company knowledge prompt/retrieval ya tuning se do.

1025.principle: Models know only what was in their training data up to a cutoff; current facts need connected sources.
1025.principle_hinglish: Model ka knowledge cutoff hota hai; naye facts ke liye live source jodo.

1026.principle: Output quality depends on the context supplied; give the model relevant specifics before considering heavier approaches.
1026.principle_hinglish: Model ko sahi context do, to jawab specific milta hai.

1027.principle: Choose the smallest model that meets quality needs; capability beyond the task adds cost and latency without value.
1027.principle_hinglish: Quality barabar ho to chhota, sasta, tez model chuno.

1028.principle: Embeddings represent meaning numerically, enabling semantic search and retrieval over content.
1028.principle_hinglish: Embeddings meaning ko numbers me badalte hain, isliye semantic search chalta hai.

1029.principle: Prompts steer model output; specificity about task, audience and format improves results.
1029.principle_hinglish: Prompt jitna clear, jawab utna kaam ka.

1030.principle: Match the model category to the transformation required, here text to image.
1030.principle_hinglish: Text se image banana ho to text-to-image model.

1031.principle: Structured data has defined fields; emails, documents, images and audio are unstructured, and gen AI can work with them directly.
1031.principle_hinglish: Table structured hota hai; email, photo, audio, PDF unstructured.

1032.principle: Data quality drives AI quality: clean, consistent, complete data first, then tune the model or prompts.
1032.principle_hinglish: Data saaf nahi to output kharab; pehle data quality sudharo.

1033.principle: Labeled data pairs examples with correct outcomes; supervised models learn from those labels.
1033.principle_hinglish: Labeled data = har example ke saath sahi jawab.

1034.principle: Models inherit and can amplify biases in training data; review data representativeness and test for fairness.
1034.principle_hinglish: Model purane biased data se seekhta hai, isliye bias aata hai.

1035.principle: Quantity is not quality: curate, version and date source content so the assistant draws on current, relevant material.
1035.principle_hinglish: Zyada data nahi, sahi aur current data chahiye.

1036.principle: Classify data and fix access controls before connecting it to AI; the assistant should honour existing permissions.
1036.principle_hinglish: AI se pehle data classify karo aur permission theek karo.

1037.principle: Unstructured, multimodal content such as video is usable when models can interpret speech, visuals and text.
1037.principle_hinglish: Video unstructured aur multimodal hota hai; model use samajh sakta hai.

1038.principle: Check whether training data represents everyone affected; missing groups yield unfair or inaccurate results.
1038.principle_hinglish: Data me kaun missing hai, ye dekho; warna unfair result.

1039.principle: Confirm legal and contractual rights and purpose limits before using data for AI.
1039.principle_hinglish: Pehle check karo ki data use karne ka haq hai ya nahi.

1040.principle: Fit data freshness to the decision; real-time facts require live data access, not a bigger model.
1040.principle_hinglish: Real-time jawab ke liye live data chahiye, purana export nahi.

1041.principle: Synthetic data supplements limited or sensitive data but must be validated against real-world conditions.
1041.principle_hinglish: Synthetic data madad karta hai, lekin real data se validate karna padta hai.

1042.principle: Good metadata improves retrieval and governance, even with capable models.
1042.principle_hinglish: Metadata se search aur trust dono behtar hote hain.

1043.principle: Model quality cannot exceed data quality; standardise and validate inputs.
1043.principle_hinglish: Garbage in, garbage out: data standard karo.

1044.principle: Minimise, mask and restrict personal data, and confirm lawful basis before using it for AI.
1044.principle_hinglish: Personal data kam karo, mask karo, access limit karo.

1045.principle: Models can generate confident but false content; verify high-stakes facts against authoritative sources.
1045.principle_hinglish: Model kabhi confident par galat (hallucination) likh sakta hai; source se verify karo.

1046.principle: Grounding lowers hallucination risk but does not remove it; keep human review proportional to stakes.
1046.principle_hinglish: Grounding se galtiyan kam hoti hain, khatam nahi; high-stakes me review rakho.

1047.principle: Systematic differences in output across groups indicate bias; test, mitigate and keep accountable humans involved.
1047.principle_hinglish: Group-wise pattern milna bias ka sanket hai; test karo aur review rakho.

1048.principle: For information newer than the model's training, provide current data at request time via grounding or retrieval.
1048.principle_hinglish: Nayi jankari ke liye grounding ya retrieval se current data do.

1049.principle: Reduce output variability with structure, examples, conservative settings and review, since some variation is inherent.
1049.principle_hinglish: Template, kam temperature aur review se variation control hota hai.

1050.principle: Treat external content as untrusted, minimise agent permissions, and add approval gates to blunt prompt injection.
1050.principle_hinglish: Bahar ke content ko untrusted maano; permission kam aur sensitive kaam par approval.

1051.principle: Overreliance is reduced by verification norms, documented assumptions and user training on limitations.
1051.principle_hinglish: Aankh band karke bharosa mat karo; check karne ki aadat dalo.

1052.principle: When explainability is limited, compensate with evidence requirements, human review and constrained autonomy.
1052.principle_hinglish: Explain na ho sake to autonomy kam aur human review zyada.

1053.principle: Verify summaries against sources, watch for omissions and fabrications, and keep human accountability in sensitive matters.
1053.principle_hinglish: Summary ko original se match karo; zimmedari insaan ki.

1054.principle: Use approved, contractually governed tools for confidential data; public consumer tools may not offer those protections.
1054.principle_hinglish: Confidential data sirf approved tools me daalo.

1055.principle: Open-ended generation requires safety filtering, policy, testing and monitoring, especially with vulnerable audiences.
1055.principle_hinglish: Open chat me safety filter aur testing zaroori hai.

1056.principle: Design tiered workflows: automate safe, common tasks and escalate ambiguous or high-stakes cases to people.
1056.principle_hinglish: Aasaan kaam automate karo, mushkil ya risky kaam insaan ko do.

1057.principle: Check provider terms, indemnity and jurisdictional IP rules, and put commercial use through legal approval.
1057.principle_hinglish: AI content ke IP rights terms aur kanoon se check karo.

1058.principle: Performance can degrade as data and behaviour change; monitor, refresh and re-evaluate continuously.
1058.principle_hinglish: Launch ke baad bhi monitoring karo, kyunki data aur behaviour badalte hain.

1059.principle: Be transparent about AI use so people can judge and challenge its output.
1059.principle_hinglish: AI use ke bare me users ko batao.

1060.principle: Evaluate on realistic, diverse inputs including edge cases, not only clean samples.
1060.principle_hinglish: Test set real-life jaisa aur diverse rakho.

1061.principle: Rank selection factors by the task: simple high-volume work favours latency and cost over maximum capability.
1061.principle_hinglish: Simple high-volume kaam me speed aur cost zyada important.

1062.principle: When errors are costly and volume is low, weight quality and context handling above unit price, and test on realistic cases.
1062.principle_hinglish: Risky aur kam volume kaam me quality pehle, price baad me.

1063.principle: Where skills and time are limited, start with managed offerings on existing models; custom training is the exception.
1063.principle_hinglish: Skills aur time kam ho to managed service use karo.

1064.principle: Match model capability to task complexity; routing can improve cost-performance at the price of added design.
1064.principle_hinglish: Kaam ke hisaab se model chuno; routing se cost aur speed balance hota hai.

1065.principle: Benchmarks inform shortlists, but company-specific evaluation on real tasks drives the choice.
1065.principle_hinglish: Benchmark shortlist ke liye, final faisla apne data par test se.

1066.principle: Modality support is a gating requirement for model choice.
1066.principle_hinglish: Photo ke liye image samajhne wala model zaroori.

1067.principle: Optimise cost by testing smaller models for simple requests and keeping stronger models for complex ones.
1067.principle_hinglish: Simple request chhote model par, mushkil par bada model.

1068.principle: Treat latency as a requirement when the workflow is time-bound, and choose models accordingly.
1068.principle_hinglish: Time-bound kaam me latency requirement hai, uske hisaab se model chuno.

1069.principle: When hosting control and deep customisation dominate, open-weight models become attractive, with added operational responsibility.
1069.principle_hinglish: Hosting control chahiye to open-weight model, par zimmedari apni.

1070.principle: Begin with the simplest approach that could work and escalate complexity only when evidence demands it.
1070.principle_hinglish: Pehle simple tareeka try karo, zarurat par complex.

1071.principle: Define use-case-specific criteria with expert review rather than relying on generic indicators.
1071.principle_hinglish: Use-case ke hisaab se criteria banao aur expert se review karao.

1072.principle: Plan for model versioning and retirement with regression tests and migration paths.
1072.principle_hinglish: Model versions retire hote hain; migration aur testing plan rakho.

1073.principle: Confirm regional processing and data-handling commitments when residency rules apply.
1073.principle_hinglish: Data kis region me process hoga, ye pehle confirm karo.

1074.principle: Compare total cost of ownership, not unit prices alone.
1074.principle_hinglish: Sirf per-token price nahi, poora cost dekho.

1075.principle: Reduce lock-in with multi-model platforms, portable prompts/evals and swappable components.
1075.principle_hinglish: Multi-model platform aur portable design se lock-in kam hota hai.

1076.principle: Gemini is Google's flagship multimodal family; Imagen is image generation, Veo is video generation, Gemma is open lightweight models.
1076.principle_hinglish: Gemini = multimodal family; Imagen = image; Veo = video; Gemma = open chhote models.

1077.principle: Use Imagen for text-to-image generation and Veo for video generation.
1077.principle_hinglish: Text se image ke liye Imagen, video ke liye Veo.

1078.principle: Match content type to family: Veo for video, Imagen for images, Gemini for multimodal understanding and generation of text.

1079.principle: Gemma offers lightweight open models for teams that want control, with added operational duty.
1079.principle_hinglish: Apne hardware par chalane wale open model ke liye Gemma.

1080.principle: Pick the model variant by task complexity, latency and cost needs.
1080.principle_hinglish: Variant task ki complexity, speed aur cost se chuno.

1081.principle: Gemini for multimodal assistants, Imagen for images, Veo for video, Gemma for open lightweight models.
1081.principle_hinglish: Gemini assistant, Imagen image, Veo video, Gemma open.

1082.principle: Small teams on tight timelines usually favour managed models; self-hosting open models suits those needing control and having the skills.
1082.principle_hinglish: Chhoti team + kam time = managed service; control chahiye to Gemma.

1083.principle: Multimodal models simplify workflows spanning text, image and audio, but still need testing and human accountability.
1083.principle_hinglish: Multimodal model ek workflow me text, image, audio sab sambhal leta hai.

1084.principle: Use models built for the required output type; 'AI' is not one interchangeable capability.
1084.principle_hinglish: Output type ke hisaab se model family chuno.

1085.principle: Review generated media for bias, likeness, safety and legal terms, and disclose synthetic content where required.
1085.principle_hinglish: Generated media publish karne se pehle review aur disclosure.

1086.principle: Keep model families (Gemini) distinct from products that use them (Gemini Enterprise, Gemini in Workspace).
1086.principle_hinglish: Gemini model hai, Gemini Enterprise product hai.

1087.principle: Govern by use case and model, with documented risk assessment and review, not by brand-level blanket approval.
1087.principle_hinglish: Brand nahi, use case aur model ke hisaab se approval do.

1088.principle: Distinguish understanding inputs from generating outputs; different tasks often use different model types.
1088.principle_hinglish: Photo samajhna aur image banana alag capabilities hain.

1089.principle: Responsible AI means declining deceptive or harmful uses even when the technology can produce them.
1089.principle_hinglish: Technology kar sakti hai matlab karna sahi nahi; deceptive use mana karo.

1091.principle: Generated visuals must be checked for accuracy so they do not mislead customers.
1091.principle_hinglish: Generated visuals sach dikhane chahiye, misleading nahi.

1092.principle: Layers: infrastructure, models, platforms, agents and applications; users meet the top layer.
1092.principle_hinglish: User ko application layer dikhti hai; neeche model aur infra hote hain.

1093.principle: Reuse commodity layers (compute, models) and invest in differentiating layers (data, workflows, applications).
1093.principle_hinglish: Commodity layers use karo, apne data aur workflow par mehnat karo.

1094.principle: Map personas and needs to different layers of offerings rather than forcing one tool on all.
1094.principle_hinglish: Persona ke hisaab se alag-alag offering chuno.

1095.principle: Inference is running a trained model to produce outputs; its cost scales with usage.
1095.principle_hinglish: Inference = trained model chalana; har use par cost.

1096.principle: Agents add tool use and multi-step orchestration to model reasoning.
1096.principle_hinglish: Agent tools use karke multi-step kaam karta hai.

1097.principle: Balance central standards and governance with controlled team-level experimentation.
1097.principle_hinglish: Central standard + controlled experiment ka balance rakho.

1098.principle: Most organisations consume and adapt existing foundation models; training one from scratch is rare.
1098.principle_hinglish: Zyadatar organisations existing model use karti hain, scratch se train nahi.

1099.principle: Enterprise offerings add security, governance, auditing and administration to model capability.
1099.principle_hinglish: Enterprise me security, governance aur admin controls zaroori.

1100.principle: Counter shadow AI by providing approved tools, clear policy, training and monitoring.
1100.principle_hinglish: Shadow AI rokne ke liye approved tool, policy aur training do.

1101.principle: Gen AI value levers include productivity, customer experience, knowledge access and innovation; measure each.
1101.principle_hinglish: Value levers: productivity, customer experience, knowledge access, innovation.

1102.principle: With shared models, advantage comes from data, integration, evaluation and adoption.
1102.principle_hinglish: Same model ho to fark data, integration aur execution se aata hai.

1103.principle: Cloud services have shared responsibility: the customer owns configuration, data and use governance.
1103.principle_hinglish: Shared responsibility: provider platform, customer apna use aur data.

1104.principle: Iterate through small pilots with measurement rather than a single big-bang launch.
1104.principle_hinglish: Chhote pilot, measure, seekho, phir expand karo.

1105.principle: An AI agent pursues goals using a model and tools, operating within limits and oversight.
1105.principle_hinglish: AI agent = goal ke liye tools use karne wala software.

1106.principle: Specialised and general models each have strengths; decide with evidence on your own data.
1106.principle_hinglish: Narrow kaam me specialised service better ho sakti hai; data par test karo.

1107.principle: Sequence adoption: governance and data, focused pilots, measure, then scale.
1107.principle_hinglish: Pehle governance aur data, phir pilot, phir scale.

1108.principle: Drive adoption with role-based training, champions and feedback loops.
1108.principle_hinglish: Role-based training aur champions se adoption badhta hai.

2001.principle: For employees who need answers from company data in a ready experience, start with the workplace offering before building custom.
2001.principle_hinglish: Employees ko company data se jawab chahiye to Gemini Enterprise jaisa workplace tool pehle dekho.

2002.principle: Enterprise assistants must respect source-system permissions; verify this before connecting sensitive repositories.
2002.principle_hinglish: Assistant wahi dikhaye jo user ko pehle se dekhne ki permission hai.

2003.principle: Enterprise workplace offerings add connectors, administration and data-handling commitments to the assistant experience.
2003.principle_hinglish: Enterprise tool me connectors, admin control aur data terms milte hain.

2004.principle: Start with configurable workplace agents for routine analyst tasks, with human approval before results are relied upon.
2004.principle_hinglish: Routine kaam ke liye low-code agent, aur output par manager ka review.

2005.principle: Begin offering selection with persona and build tolerance; employees plus no software building suggests a ready workplace assistant.
2005.principle_hinglish: Pehle dekho user kaun hai aur build karna hai ya nahi.

2006.principle: Sustained adoption comes from role-specific use cases, connected data and training, not from raising model capability alone.
2006.principle_hinglish: Adoption role-wise use case, data connection aur training se badhta hai.

2007.principle: Pair employee-facing needs with workplace offerings and custom product features with the developer platform.
2007.principle_hinglish: Employee tool aur customer app feature ke liye alag layers.

2008.principle: Procurement for workplace AI should examine retention, data use, residency and auditing, not features alone.
2008.principle_hinglish: Procurement me data retention, use aur audit ke sawal pucho.

2009.principle: Position workplace AI as an accelerator whose outputs are verified by accountable people.
2009.principle_hinglish: AI ko accelerator maano; facts ki zimmedari analyst ki.

2010.principle: Workplace agents combine connected data, summarisation and drafting, leaving the person to review and decide.
2010.principle_hinglish: Agent data jodta, summary banata, draft likhta hai; faisla insaan ka.

2011.principle: Report what the pilot proved, scale where value is shown, and set new measures for outcomes still unproven.
2011.principle_hinglish: Jo pilot me saabit hua wahi claim karo; baaki ke liye naye measures.

2012.principle: Correct access permissions and data classification before connecting repositories to AI assistants.
2012.principle_hinglish: Repository jodne se pehle permissions theek karo.

2013.principle: Test multilingual quality on real languages and documents when staff work across regions.
2013.principle_hinglish: Multilingual quality apni languages me test karo.

2014.principle: Gemini names the models; Gemini Enterprise is a workplace product for employees.
2014.principle_hinglish: Gemini model hai; Gemini Enterprise employees ke liye product.

2015.principle: Govern self-built agents with creation permissions, least-privilege data access and approval gates for external actions.
2015.principle_hinglish: Agent banane, data access aur bahar bhejne par controls rakho.

2016.principle: For everyday productivity in tools people already use, choose the AI built into those tools.
2016.principle_hinglish: Roz ke apps me AI chahiye to Workspace wala Gemini.

2017.principle: Pair built-in meeting assistance with clear policy on usage and human review of the notes.
2017.principle_hinglish: Meet ke built-in features use karo, par policy aur review ke saath.

2018.principle: In-app productivity help and cross-repository answers are different needs and may use different offerings.
2018.principle_hinglish: In-app help aur cross-system search alag needs hain.

2019.principle: AI help inside spreadsheets reduces skill barriers, but users must validate outputs against known figures.
2019.principle_hinglish: Formula help milti hai par result khud verify karo.

2020.principle: Check data-handling terms and regulatory fit before using AI drafting with sensitive communications.
2020.principle_hinglish: Sensitive data me pehle privacy terms check karo.

2021.principle: When answers must come only from provided documents, choose a source-grounded tool with citations.
2021.principle_hinglish: Sirf diye gaye documents se jawab chahiye to source-grounded tool.

2022.principle: Grow adoption with role-based, task-specific enablement and shared success stories.
2022.principle_hinglish: Role-wise practical training se adoption badhta hai.

2023.principle: Use built-in AI for common productivity; build governed, integrated solutions for regulated customer-facing products.
2023.principle_hinglish: Productivity ke liye built-in, regulated customer product ke liye custom build.

2024.principle: For code writing and review help inside developer tools, choose a coding assistant.
2024.principle_hinglish: Developers ke liye coding assistant jaisa tool.

2025.principle: AI drafting speeds first versions, but people refine for accuracy and brand and approve before release.
2025.principle_hinglish: AI first draft banata hai; brand aur accuracy insaan dekhta hai.

2026.principle: Administrative controls over who can use AI features are essential for policy compliance.
2026.principle_hinglish: Kaun AI use kar sakta hai, ye admin control se tay hota hai.

2027.principle: Confirm data-use terms and settings in writing rather than relying on assumptions or reputation.
2027.principle_hinglish: Data use terms khud verify karo aur document karo.

2028.principle: Estimate ROI from measured task-level baselines rather than vendor claims or usage counts.
2028.principle_hinglish: ROI task-level before/after measure se nikalo.

2029.principle: Meeting captions and translation features address multilingual participation inside collaboration tools.
2029.principle_hinglish: Meeting me captions aur translation language barrier hataate hain.

2030.principle: Use Model Garden to discover and compare Google, third-party and open models on the developer platform.
2030.principle_hinglish: Kai models compare karne ke liye Model Garden.

2031.principle: When you need a customised, integrated and auditable AI feature in your own product, build on the developer platform.
2031.principle_hinglish: Custom, integrated aur auditable feature ke liye developer platform.

2032.principle: When consistent style or format is needed and prompting has plateaued, consider tuning on the platform.
2032.principle_hinglish: Prompt se baat na bane to style ke liye tuning.

2033.principle: Use evaluation tooling with your own test cases to compare candidate models systematically.
2033.principle_hinglish: Apne test cases par evaluation karke models compare karo.

2034.principle: Small teams on tight timelines usually start managed; open deployment suits strong control needs and available skills.
2034.principle_hinglish: Chhoti team, kam time: managed pehle, control ki zarurat par open.

2035.principle: Developer platform = build custom applications; productivity AI = ready-made help in everyday tools.
2035.principle_hinglish: Platform build karne ke liye; productivity AI ready-made help.

2036.principle: For approved-source answers, ground the model in the approved documents and expose citations.
2036.principle_hinglish: Approved documents me ground karo aur citation dikhao.

2037.principle: Design for swappable models with portable prompts and evaluation sets.
2037.principle_hinglish: Model swap karne layak design rakho.

2038.principle: Production AI needs access control, data protection, monitoring and auditing in addition to model quality.
2038.principle_hinglish: Production ke liye access control, monitoring aur audit zaroori.

2039.principle: Scale prototypes with representative evaluation, content pipelines, monitoring and feedback loops.
2039.principle_hinglish: Scale ke liye evaluation, content update, monitoring aur feedback.

2040.principle: Use current official terminology and note legacy names; verify against current documentation.
2040.principle_hinglish: Current official naming use karo, purana naam ek baar note karo.

2041.principle: Use the catalog to shortlist by task, size and cost, then test on your own labeled sample.
2041.principle_hinglish: Catalog se shortlist, phir apne sample par test.

2042.principle: Actions on business systems require tool use with orchestration and guardrails.
2042.principle_hinglish: System me action ke liye tool use aur guardrails chahiye.

2043.principle: Control cost by matching model size to task, trimming tokens and monitoring cost per outcome.
2043.principle_hinglish: Cost control: chhota model, kam tokens, monitoring.

2044.principle: Agent Studio supports low-code agent design on the enterprise platform; Google AI Studio is a different developer tool.
2044.principle_hinglish: Low-code agent design ke liye Agent Studio; AI Studio alag tool hai.

2045.principle: Use low-code to validate and learn quickly; bring developers in for integrations, controls and production hardening.
2045.principle_hinglish: Low-code se validate karo, production ke liye developers.

2046.principle: Agent Studio (low-code agent design on the enterprise platform) and Google AI Studio (developer prototyping) are distinct.
2046.principle_hinglish: Agent Studio aur AI Studio alag hain.

2047.principle: Govern low-code agents with owners, review criteria and lifecycle management.
2047.principle_hinglish: Low-code agents ke owner, review aur lifecycle tay karo.

2048.principle: Prototype quickly with low-code and a small user group before committing engineering investment.

2049.principle: Keep agents narrowly scoped with defined tools and human escalation for edge cases.
2049.principle_hinglish: Agent ka scope chhota rakho aur escalation rakho.

2050.principle: Constrain agents to approved knowledge, require citations and allow them to say when they do not know.
2050.principle_hinglish: Approved knowledge tak seemit rakho, citation do, 'pata nahi' allow karo.

2051.principle: Test agents on representative and edge-case scenarios in a safe environment, with approval gates before real actions.
2051.principle_hinglish: Agent ko safe environment me edge cases ke saath test karo.

2052.principle: Enable local building with approved templates, managed data connections and central guardrails.

2053.principle: Agents pursue goals across steps with tools and data; FAQ bots return prepared answers.
2053.principle_hinglish: Agent tools se multi-step kaam karta hai; FAQ bot sirf fixed jawab.

2054.principle: Prefer configuration for standard Q&A tasks, with escalation rules and review of interactions.
2054.principle_hinglish: Standard Q&A ke liye configure karo; escalation aur review rakho.

2055.principle: When you need grounded search and answers over your own content with minimal build effort, consider Agent Search.
2055.principle_hinglish: Apne content par grounded search ke liye Agent Search.

2056.principle: Prefer managed search when needs are standard and resources are limited; build custom retrieval when special control is required.
2056.principle_hinglish: Standard need aur kam resource: managed search; special control par custom.

2057.principle: Grounded answers should expose citations, and high-stakes use should be verified by accountable people.
2057.principle_hinglish: Citation dikhao aur high-stakes me attorney verify kare.

2058.principle: Retail product discovery with intent-based queries calls for AI commerce search and recommendation capabilities.
2058.principle_hinglish: Retail product search ke liye AI commerce search.

2059.principle: Search is only as good as its content; curate, version and assign owners.
2059.principle_hinglish: Search content jitna accha hoga result utna accha.

2060.principle: Enterprise search must enforce document-level access rights for each user.
2060.principle_hinglish: Search me har user ke access rights lagne chahiye.

2061.principle: Match search or assistant offerings to audience and content source, keeping public and internal content separate.
2061.principle_hinglish: Public aur internal content alag rakho.

2062.principle: Evaluate search with representative questions, expert-approved answers and feedback tracking.
2062.principle_hinglish: Real questions aur expert answers se search evaluate karo.

2063.principle: Grounded search retrieves sources first, then generates, enabling citations.
2063.principle_hinglish: Pehle retrieve, phir generate: isliye citation milta hai.

2064.principle: Use grounded multilingual search over existing content, and test quality in the main languages.
2064.principle_hinglish: Multilingual question, grounded English content, languages me test.

2065.principle: Start with managed search, measure, and customise only where gaps are proven.
2065.principle_hinglish: Pehle managed search, phir zarurat par custom.

2066.principle: Clinical search answers need citations, versions and a reminder that professional judgment stays with the clinician.
2066.principle_hinglish: Clinical answer me citation, version aur clinician ka judgment.

2067.principle: Going from answering to acting requires agent capabilities with integrations, permissions, confirmations and audit.
2067.principle_hinglish: Answer se action tak jaane ke liye agent, permissions aur audit.

2068.principle: For customer-facing conversational self-service with human escalation, use customer engagement offerings.
2068.principle_hinglish: Customer-facing self-service aur human handoff ke liye customer engagement offering.

2069.principle: Agent-assist capabilities help human contact-centre staff in real time; automation replaces them only where chosen.
2069.principle_hinglish: Human agent ko live suggestions dene wala agent-assist.

2070.principle: Conversation analytics turns contact-centre interactions into topic, sentiment and driver insights.
2070.principle_hinglish: Calls aur chats ka analytics reasons batata hai.

2071.principle: Customer-facing bots need clear human escalation with context passed along, especially for sensitive cases.
2071.principle_hinglish: Bot me human escalation aur context handoff zaroori.

2072.principle: Voice self-service combines speech recognition, conversational understanding and speech synthesis.

2073.principle: Automate low-risk, well-defined requests with controls; route sensitive or complex cases to humans.
2073.principle_hinglish: Risk ke hisaab se automate karo; sensitive cases human ko.

2074.principle: Ground customer-service agents in maintained sources instead of retraining for changing facts.
2074.principle_hinglish: Policies badalti hain: knowledge base se ground karo.

2075.principle: Evaluate customer agents on resolution, satisfaction, escalation causes and sampled accuracy, not on containment alone.
2075.principle_hinglish: Containment ke saath satisfaction aur accuracy bhi naapo.

2076.principle: Protect personal data in customer conversations with authentication, access limits, retention and redaction.
2076.principle_hinglish: Authentication, limited access aur retention/redaction rakho.

2077.principle: Treat safety-relevant answers such as allergy details as high-stakes: verified sources and escalation.
2077.principle_hinglish: Allergy jaise safety answers verified data se aur escalation ke saath.

2078.principle: For resident or customer service across channels with a small team, configure a customer engagement offering.
2078.principle_hinglish: Small IT team: customer engagement offering configure karo.

2079.principle: Personalise only with consent, lawful basis and authentication.
2079.principle_hinglish: Consent aur authentication ke baad hi personalisation.

2080.principle: Handle peaks by automating common requests while escalating complex ones and monitoring quality.
2080.principle_hinglish: Peak me common requests automate, complex human ko.

2081.principle: For narrow, well-defined tasks such as transcription, a purpose-built API is often the simplest, cheapest and most predictable option.
2081.principle_hinglish: Narrow kaam (transcription) ke liye purpose-built API sabse simple.

2082.principle: Use document-processing services for classifying documents and extracting structured data at scale.
2082.principle_hinglish: Scanned forms se fields nikalne ke liye document processing service.

2083.principle: High-volume, well-defined translation with brand-term consistency suits a purpose-built translation service.
2083.principle_hinglish: High-volume translation glossary ke saath: translation API.

2084.principle: For narrow, high-volume tasks, compare specialised services with general models on your own labeled data.
2084.principle_hinglish: Narrow high-volume kaam me specialised aur general model ko apne data par compare karo.

2085.principle: Text-to-speech converts text to spoken audio; speech-to-text does the opposite.
2085.principle_hinglish: Text se audio: text-to-speech; audio se text: speech-to-text.

2086.principle: For large-scale structured tagging, compare purpose-built language analysis with prompted generative models on a labeled sample.
2086.principle_hinglish: Structured tagging ke liye sample par dono approaches compare karo.

2087.principle: Compose specialised services, rules and generative models, and keep a person at consequential decision points.
2087.principle_hinglish: Extraction, rules, drafting alag components; decision par insaan.

2088.principle: Image-content checks use vision capabilities; confirm borderline cases with human moderators.
2088.principle_hinglish: Image analysis ke liye vision capability.

2089.principle: For fixed, repeatable extraction, prioritise consistency, accuracy and auditability over flexibility.
2089.principle_hinglish: Fixed extraction me consistency aur audit sabse important.

2090.principle: Captioning is based on speech recognition (speech-to-text).

2091.principle: At high volume on a narrow task, benchmark specialised services against general models on accuracy, latency and cost.
2091.principle_hinglish: High-volume narrow task me specialised service benchmark karo.

2092.principle: Use managed purpose-built APIs for mature capabilities and focus scarce engineers on what differentiates.
2092.principle_hinglish: Mature capabilities ke liye API, engineers unique features par.

2093.principle: Check data terms, security, residency and consent before sending sensitive audio to any service.
2093.principle_hinglish: Sensitive audio bhejne se pehle data terms, security aur consent.

2094.principle: Use purpose-built APIs for narrow stable tasks and generative models for open-ended ones, then validate by testing.
2094.principle_hinglish: Narrow stable: API; open-ended: generative; phir test.

2095.principle: Agents use tools and data to pursue goals across multiple steps; plain chat models mostly generate text.
2095.principle_hinglish: Agent tools use karke multi-step kaam karta hai.

2096.principle: Constrain agents with least privilege, approvals for consequential actions and complete logging.
2096.principle_hinglish: Agent ko kam permission, payment par approval aur logging.

2097.principle: Orchestration coordinates tasks, context and failures across agents and tools.
2097.principle_hinglish: Agents ke beech coordination ko orchestration kehte hain.

2098.principle: Treat outside content as untrusted, minimise agent authority, and require approvals for consequential actions.
2098.principle_hinglish: Bahar ka content untrusted; authority kam; approval zaroori.

2099.principle: Evaluate agents end to end on realistic tasks, covering routing, tool errors, escalation and cost.
2099.principle_hinglish: Agent ko end-to-end realistic tasks par test karo.

2100.principle: Scale agent autonomy with the risk of the action; consequential changes get human approval.
2100.principle_hinglish: Risk ke hisaab se autonomy; payroll par approval.

2101.principle: Make agents retrieve and display real sources, and verify key claims before relying on them.
2101.principle_hinglish: Agent real sources retrieve kare aur scientist verify kare.

2102.principle: Give agents tools that query live systems for time-sensitive facts.
2102.principle_hinglish: Time-sensitive facts ke liye live system tool.

2103.principle: Have agents propose and explain, and keep qualified people accountable for acceptance.
2103.principle_hinglish: Agent propose kare, lawyer approve kare.

2104.principle: Control agent cost by simplifying steps, right-sizing models, caching and tracking cost per task.
2104.principle_hinglish: Agent cost: steps kam, chhota model, caching, monitoring.

2105.principle: Agents need observability: tracing of prompts, tool calls and sources for debugging and audit.
2105.principle_hinglish: Agent ke steps ka tracing aur logging zaroori.

2106.principle: Prefer focused agents with clear scopes, tools and escalation over one sprawling agent.
2106.principle_hinglish: Ek bada agent nahi, focused agents with clear scope.

2107.principle: Favour open interoperability standards and documented interfaces for multi-vendor agent ecosystems.
2107.principle_hinglish: Multi-vendor agents ke liye open standards.

2108.principle: Map each need to the layer matching its audience and customisation level: productivity AI, developer platform, or purpose-built API.
2108.principle_hinglish: Har need ko uske layer se match karo.

2109.principle: For everyday drafting in familiar tools, choose built-in productivity AI before custom builds.
2109.principle_hinglish: Roz ke tools me drafting ke liye built-in AI.

2110.principle: Choose a workplace assistant when employees need permission-aware, cited answers from internal repositories without building software.
2110.principle_hinglish: Employees ko internal repositories se cited answers: workplace assistant.

2111.principle: A branded, integrated, customer-facing feature belongs on the developer platform.
2111.principle_hinglish: Branded customer feature ke liye developer platform.

2112.principle: For consistent, auditable extraction at volume from forms, choose document-processing services.
2112.principle_hinglish: Forms se fields nikalne ke liye document processing.

2113.principle: For changing, citeable knowledge with a small team, choose managed grounded search over tuning.
2113.principle_hinglish: Hafte-wise badalte docs: grounded search, tuning nahi.

2114.principle: For customer chat and voice with system actions and handoff, choose customer engagement offerings.
2114.principle_hinglish: Passenger chat/voice ke liye customer engagement offering.

2115.principle: For questions over a small, specific document set with citations, use a source-grounded notebook tool.
2115.principle_hinglish: Chhote document set par citation ke saath: source-grounded notebook.

2116.principle: Match tooling to maturity and control needs: low-code for experiments, platform for governed production, open hosting only where justified.
2116.principle_hinglish: Experiment: low-code; production: platform; open hosting sirf jahan zaroori.

2117.principle: Test candidate approaches on a labeled multilingual sample and choose on accuracy and cost.
2117.principle_hinglish: Multilingual labeled sample par test karke choose karo.

2118.principle: Prototype with low-code or managed tools before committing engineering or large licences.

2119.principle: For shopper intent-based search and recommendation over a catalog, choose AI commerce search.
2119.principle_hinglish: Shopper intent ke search ke liye commerce search.

2120.principle: With standard use cases and scarce developers, configure a ready product first and customise where gaps are proven.
2120.principle_hinglish: Standard needs aur kam developers: configurable product pehle.

2121.principle: To compare many models under the same conditions, use a multi-model catalog with evaluation tooling.
2121.principle_hinglish: Models compare karne ke liye multi-model catalog aur evaluation.

2122.principle: Use video-generation models for promos and keep creative and legal review before release.
2122.principle_hinglish: Video promo ke liye video model, release se pehle review.

2123.principle: For multi-repository search, weigh connector coverage and permission-aware access most heavily.
2123.principle_hinglish: Multi-repository search me permission-aware access sabse zaroori.

2124.principle: For high-stakes drafting, use capable, grounded models with citations and expert review.
2124.principle_hinglish: High-stakes drafting: grounded model, citation, expert review.

2125.principle: Routine, stable-pattern questions with a maintained knowledge base suit grounded conversational agents with escalation.
2125.principle_hinglish: Routine questions: grounded conversational agent with escalation.

2126.principle: Frame the portfolio by persona and need, matching each to the right layer of offering, under common governance.
2126.principle_hinglish: Persona aur need ke hisaab se layers; common governance.

3001.principle: Start with prompt design: state task, audience, tone, format and the specific content required.
3001.principle_hinglish: Pehle prompt me task, audience, tone aur format batao.

3002.principle: Few-shot examples improve consistency of format and labels without any retraining.
3002.principle_hinglish: Few-shot examples se format aur labels consistent hote hain.

3003.principle: Tell the model who the reader is and what the text must achieve to control tone and complexity.
3003.principle_hinglish: Reader aur goal batane se style sahi aata hai.

3004.principle: For multi-step problems, request step-by-step reasoning and verify the working.
3004.principle_hinglish: Multi-step problem me step-by-step reasoning maango aur verify karo.

3005.principle: Specify the exact output format when results feed other systems.
3005.principle_hinglish: Downstream system ke liye exact output format specify karo.

3006.principle: Prompting is iterative: refine with context, constraints and examples, and compare.

3007.principle: Write explicit rules and escalation paths in prompts, and enforce limits with controls outside the model.
3007.principle_hinglish: Prompt me rules likho aur limits system level par bhi lagao.

3008.principle: Tell the model to use only supplied text, quote it, and admit gaps.
3008.principle_hinglish: Sirf diye gaye text se jawab do aur gap batao.

3009.principle: Create tested, shared prompt templates to raise and standardise quality.

3010.principle: Compare prompt versions on a representative test set using defined criteria.
3010.principle_hinglish: Prompt versions ko test set aur criteria par compare karo.

3011.principle: Ground answers in the maintained source when facts are specific and change over time.
3011.principle_hinglish: Badalte facts ke liye maintained source me ground karo.

3012.principle: Grounding reduces but does not eliminate errors; keep oversight in proportion to the stakes.
3012.principle_hinglish: Grounding se galti kam hoti hai, khatam nahi.

3013.principle: For information newer than the model's training, ground in live sources.
3013.principle_hinglish: Nayi khabar ke liye live source me ground karo.

3014.principle: Citations make grounded answers verifiable and build reviewer trust.
3014.principle_hinglish: Citation se claims verify ho sakte hain.

3015.principle: Evaluate claim-to-source faithfulness and improve retrieval and instructions; a real citation is not proof of a correct claim.
3015.principle_hinglish: Citation sahi hone se claim sahi nahi hota; faithfulness check karo.

3016.principle: For changing, citeable facts, ground at answer time instead of tuning.
3016.principle_hinglish: Changing citeable facts: grounding tuning se behtar.

3017.principle: Ground in governed enterprise data sources when answers depend on private content.
3017.principle_hinglish: Private content ke liye governed enterprise data grounding.

3018.principle: When grounded answers miss existing content, check retrieval (indexing, chunking, ranking) first.
3018.principle_hinglish: Content milta nahi to pehle retrieval check karo.

3019.principle: Grounding connects model output to trusted sources.
3019.principle_hinglish: Grounding = jawab ko trusted source se jodna.

3020.principle: Enforce access rights in retrieval so grounding never exposes restricted content.

3021.principle: Use RAG when content is large, changing and must be cited.
3021.principle_hinglish: Large, badalta, citeable content ke liye RAG.

3022.principle: In RAG, retrieval quality (chunking, metadata, ranking) limits answer quality; test it directly.
3022.principle_hinglish: RAG me retrieval quality sabse important: chunking aur metadata.

3023.principle: If the content fits in context and the use is small, direct inclusion can beat building RAG; RAG scales to large or shared corpora.
3023.principle_hinglish: Chhota content context me fit ho to seedha daalo; bade corpus ke liye RAG.

3024.principle: Keep RAG indexes as fresh as the underlying facts change, or query the live source.
3024.principle_hinglish: Data jitna fast badle, index utna fresh rakho.

3025.principle: RAG suits changing content and limited labeled data; tuning needs examples and refresh effort.
3025.principle_hinglish: Content change aur labeled data kam: RAG.

3026.principle: Apply access control in retrieval, not just in prompts.
3026.principle_hinglish: Retrieval level par access control lagao.

3027.principle: Diagnose RAG failures by checking retrieval relevance and generation faithfulness separately.
3027.principle_hinglish: RAG failure me retrieval aur generation alag check karo.

3028.principle: RAG retrieves relevant content first, then generates from it.

3029.principle: Combine RAG for changing facts with prompting or tuning for style.
3029.principle_hinglish: Facts ke liye RAG, style ke liye prompt ya tuning.

3030.principle: Enforce role-based access, minimise indexed sensitive fields and log access in RAG over personal data.
3030.principle_hinglish: Personal data par RAG me role-based access aur logging.

3031.principle: Tuning fits consistent style, format or domain behaviour when prompting is not enough and examples exist.
3031.principle_hinglish: Style aur format ki consistency ke liye examples se tuning.

3032.principle: Do not tune to keep fast-changing facts current; retrieve or ground instead.
3032.principle_hinglish: Fast-changing facts ke liye tuning nahi, retrieval.

3033.principle: Tuning needs curated, consistent, high-quality examples.
3033.principle_hinglish: Tuning ke liye curated high-quality examples.

3034.principle: Tune when the benefit justifies the data, effort and maintenance; otherwise keep improving prompts.
3034.principle_hinglish: Tuning tabhi jab fayda effort se zyada ho.

3035.principle: Specialised vocabulary and behaviour with labeled data is a good candidate for tuning, compared against prompt-based fixes.
3035.principle_hinglish: Domain terminology + labeled data: tuning evaluate karo.

3036.principle: Treat tuning data as sensitive data use: lawful basis, de-identification, controls and leakage testing.
3036.principle_hinglish: Tuning data bhi sensitive data use hai.

3037.principle: Tuned behaviour is a snapshot; re-evaluate and refresh as needs change.
3037.principle_hinglish: Tuning snapshot hai; guidelines badle to refresh karo.

3038.principle: Use tuning (or examples) for style and behaviour, and retrieval or prompts for case-specific facts.
3038.principle_hinglish: Style ke liye tuning, facts ke liye retrieval.

3039.principle: Evaluate tuned models on held-out data and compare with a baseline before deployment.
3039.principle_hinglish: Tuned model ko held-out data par baseline se compare karo.

3040.principle: Tuning adapts a pre-trained model with extra examples; it isn't training from scratch or just prompting.
3040.principle_hinglish: Tuning = pre-trained model ko examples se adapt karna.

3041.principle: Retrieve live data at request time; use prompting or tuning for stable tone.
3041.principle_hinglish: Live data retrieve karo, tone prompt/tuning se.

3042.principle: Raise temperature for creative variety and lower it for consistency; settings change variability, not knowledge.
3042.principle_hinglish: Creative kaam me temperature zyada, consistent text me kam.

3043.principle: Temperature changes consistency, not truthfulness; use grounding, evaluation and review for accuracy.
3043.principle_hinglish: Temperature zero bhi galti rok nahi sakta.

3044.principle: Max output length limits answer size and cost; too low truncates, so combine with concise prompting.
3044.principle_hinglish: Max output tokens length aur cost control karta hai.

3045.principle: Top-p and top-k restrict the candidate words sampled, influencing variety along with temperature.
3045.principle_hinglish: Top-p candidate words ka set limit karta hai.

3046.principle: Use prompt structure and examples for format; use settings to tune variability.
3046.principle_hinglish: Format prompt aur example se, variability settings se.

3047.principle: For repeatability, lower randomness, fix instructions, test repeated runs and log results.
3047.principle_hinglish: Repeatability ke liye low temperature, fixed instructions aur testing.

3048.principle: Use task-specific settings and prompts rather than one global configuration.
3048.principle_hinglish: Har task ke liye alag settings.

3049.principle: Stop sequences and length limits control where generation ends.
3049.principle_hinglish: Stop sequence output kahan khatam ho ye batata hai.

3050.principle: Evaluate settings on representative cases against agreed criteria.
3050.principle_hinglish: Settings ko representative set par evaluate karo.

3051.principle: Conservative settings aren't a hallucination cure; add grounding, verification and review.
3051.principle_hinglish: Conservative settings hallucination khatam nahi karte.

3052.principle: Evaluate with a representative test set, explicit criteria and human scoring before launch.
3052.principle_hinglish: Real tickets ka test set, criteria aur human scoring.

3053.principle: Combine automated metrics with expert review aimed at high-risk errors such as critical omissions.
3053.principle_hinglish: Metric ke saath expert review, critical omissions par focus.

3054.principle: Judge accuracy against a baseline and the severity of errors, not as an absolute number.
3054.principle_hinglish: Accuracy ko baseline aur error severity ke saath dekho.

3055.principle: Keep a held-out evaluation set that is not used for tuning prompts or models.
3055.principle_hinglish: Held-out set alag rakho jo tuning me use na ho.

3056.principle: Evaluate safety with adversarial tests and keep monitoring after launch.
3056.principle_hinglish: Safety ke liye adversarial testing aur monitoring.

3057.principle: Use model-based grading only after calibrating against human judgments, keeping human review for high stakes.
3057.principle_hinglish: Model grader ko human labels se calibrate karo.

3058.principle: Evaluate both answer quality and business outcomes.
3058.principle_hinglish: Accuracy ke saath business outcomes bhi naapo.

3059.principle: Involve domain experts with clear rubrics in evaluation.
3059.principle_hinglish: Domain experts aur rubric se evaluation.

3060.principle: Run regression tests including rare cases on every change, and monitor in production.
3060.principle_hinglish: Har change par regression test aur monitoring.

3061.principle: Use controlled experiments to measure business impact.
3061.principle_hinglish: Business impact ke liye controlled experiment.

3062.principle: Collect structured feedback, review failures and feed hard cases into the test set.
3062.principle_hinglish: Feedback collect karo aur hard cases test set me daalo.

3063.principle: Use retrieval for changing, citeable facts and prompt examples for format; tune only if prompting can't deliver consistency.
3063.principle_hinglish: Changing facts: retrieval; format: prompt examples.

3064.principle: Use tuning for consistent voice and retrieval for facts that change.
3064.principle_hinglish: Voice ke liye tuning, facts ke liye retrieval.

3065.principle: Start with prompting (and basic grounding); add heavier techniques only when evidence shows a need.
3065.principle_hinglish: Pehle sabse simple technique try karo.

3066.principle: Map each requirement to its lever: retrieval for fresh cited facts, prompts and guardrails for scope, examples or tuning for style.
3066.principle_hinglish: Har requirement ko sahi lever se match karo.

3067.principle: Try cheaper, reversible techniques (prompting) before heavier ones (retrieval, tuning), guided by evidence.
3067.principle_hinglish: Pehle sasta aur reversible, phir heavy.

3068.principle: For answers limited to specific documents with citations, use retrieval or grounding.

3069.principle: Diagnose the problem type first: format issues are addressed by prompts or tuning, not retrieval.
3069.principle_hinglish: Problem type pehchano: format issue = prompt/tuning.

3070.principle: Choose the technique that fits freshness, traceability and maintenance constraints, not the most advanced.
3070.principle_hinglish: Advanced hone se behtar nahi; constraints ke hisaab se chuno.

3071.principle: Tune for specialised language and behaviour; use live retrieval for volatile facts.
3071.principle_hinglish: Jargon ke liye tuning, live facts ke liye retrieval.

3072.principle: No technique eliminates errors; choose by need and keep review proportional to stakes.
3072.principle_hinglish: Koi technique galti khatam nahi karti.

4001.principle: Select pilots by scoring value, feasibility, data readiness and risk, not by enthusiasm or seniority.
4001.principle_hinglish: Value, feasibility, data readiness aur risk se pilot chuno.

4002.principle: Build ROI from measured baselines, realistic conversion of time to value, and full costs.
4002.principle_hinglish: ROI baseline, realistic value conversion aur full cost se nikalo.

4003.principle: Drive adoption through involvement, clear communication on role changes, training and champions.
4003.principle_hinglish: Adoption ke liye involvement, communication aur training.

4004.principle: Design pilots with baselines, defined groups and time frames, and metrics on value and risk.
4004.principle_hinglish: Pilot ke pehle metrics aur baseline tay karo.

4005.principle: Buy or configure for standard needs; build where differentiation justifies the cost.

4006.principle: Establish cross-functional governance with decision rights, a risk review process and shared measures.
4006.principle_hinglish: Cross-functional governance aur decision rights banao.

4007.principle: Scale in phases with cost modelling, training, support, monitoring and governance.
4007.principle_hinglish: Scale phased karo: cost, training, monitoring, governance.

4008.principle: Track adoption, quality, risk and business outcomes together.
4008.principle_hinglish: Adoption, quality, risk aur business impact saath me.

4009.principle: Build AI literacy broadly and combine domain experts with a small specialist core.
4009.principle_hinglish: Broad AI literacy aur kuch specialists.

4010.principle: Pick bounded, internal, human-reviewed tasks for early wins.
4010.principle_hinglish: Early wins: bounded, internal, reviewed tasks.

4011.principle: Compare vendors on your own tasks plus security, data terms, support and total cost.
4011.principle_hinglish: Apne tasks par vendors test karo, terms aur total cost dekho.

4012.principle: Consolidate overlapping pilots, reuse components, and fund by evidence.
4012.principle_hinglish: Overlap hatao, reuse karo, evidence par fund karo.

4013.principle: Responsible AI in hiring needs fairness testing, transparency and human accountability.
4013.principle_hinglish: Hiring me fairness test, transparency aur human accountability.

4014.principle: Be transparent about AI use, base explanations on real criteria, and keep humans accountable.
4014.principle_hinglish: AI use batao, reasons real criteria se, accountability bank ki.

4015.principle: Run impact assessments covering harms, bias, privacy and oversight before launch.
4015.principle_hinglish: Launch se pehle impact assessment karo.

4016.principle: Keep named human owners accountable, with appeal routes and records.

4017.principle: Measure outcomes across groups, investigate, mitigate and monitor continuously.
4017.principle_hinglish: Groups ke outcomes naapo, jaanch karo, sudharo, monitor karo.

4018.principle: Avoid deception, follow disclosure rules and review synthetic content.
4018.principle_hinglish: Synthetic content ko real mat dikhao, disclosure follow karo.

4019.principle: Use safety filters, red-teaming, monitoring and reporting for open-ended characters.

4020.principle: Operationalise AI principles through reviews, risk tiers, training and accountable owners.

4021.principle: Minimise data, set consent and retention limits, and restrict access from the start.

4022.principle: Provide checkable reasons and state limitations to support appropriate reliance.
4022.principle_hinglish: Checkable reasons do aur limitations batao.

4023.principle: Test with diverse groups, improve accessibility and language support, and keep alternative channels.
4023.principle_hinglish: Diverse groups ke saath test, accessibility aur alternative channels.

4024.principle: Use approved enterprise tools with data-protection terms, lawful basis and access controls for sensitive data.
4024.principle_hinglish: Sensitive data ke liye approved enterprise tool aur lawful basis.

4025.principle: Apply least privilege through permission-aware retrieval and careful repository connection.

4026.principle: Verify regional processing and storage commitments, controls and audit evidence.
4026.principle_hinglish: Region ke processing aur storage commitments verify karo.

4027.principle: Confirm training-use and retention terms in the contract and settings, and document them.
4027.principle_hinglish: Training use aur retention terms contract me check karo.

4028.principle: Mask personal identifiers, restrict access and log use before analysing customer data.
4028.principle_hinglish: Personal identifiers mask karo, access limit karo.

4029.principle: Counter shadow AI with an approved alternative, clear policy and training, and technical controls.
4029.principle_hinglish: Approved alternative, policy, training aur technical controls.

4030.principle: Balance auditability and privacy through redaction, restricted access and defined retention.
4030.principle_hinglish: Audit aur privacy ka balance: redaction, access aur retention.

4031.principle: Manage third-party AI risk with due diligence, contract terms, minimised sharing and incident response plans.
4031.principle_hinglish: Third-party risk: due diligence, contract, minimisation, incident plan.

4032.principle: Fix over-shared permissions before connecting an assistant; AI makes exposure easier to find.
4032.principle_hinglish: Over-sharing pehle theek karo, phir assistant connect karo.

4033.principle: Expect encryption, IAM, audit logging, network controls and relevant compliance attestations.
4033.principle_hinglish: Encryption, IAM, audit logging, network controls aur certifications.

4034.principle: Classify data into tiers and map each tier to approved tools.
4034.principle_hinglish: Data tiers banao aur har tier ke liye approved tools tay karo.

4035.principle: SAIF is a conceptual framework for securing AI systems across the lifecycle; adopt it as practice, not as a product.
4035.principle_hinglish: SAIF AI systems ko secure karne ka framework hai, product nahi.

4036.principle: Treat outside content as untrusted, limit permissions, and approve sensitive actions.
4036.principle_hinglish: Bahar ka content untrusted, permissions limit, sensitive par approval.

4037.principle: Protect training pipelines with data provenance, validation, monitoring and drift detection.
4037.principle_hinglish: Training data ka provenance aur validation rakho.

4038.principle: Vet, test, version and permission-limit third-party models and plug-ins.
4038.principle_hinglish: Third-party models aur plug-ins ko vet aur test karo.

4039.principle: Treat model output as untrusted: review, test and sandbox before use.
4039.principle_hinglish: Model output ko untrusted maano: review aur test.

4040.principle: Red-team before launch with adversarial tests, then fix and retest.

4041.principle: Monitor prompts, flags, tool use, data access, costs and reports, not just uptime.
4041.principle_hinglish: Uptime ke alawa abuse signals bhi monitor karo.

4042.principle: Protect valuable models with authentication, rate limits, monitoring and access controls.
4042.principle_hinglish: Model API par authentication, rate limits aur monitoring.

4043.principle: Under shared responsibility the customer still secures its configuration, access, data and usage.
4043.principle_hinglish: Provider platform secure karta hai, customer config aur use.

4044.principle: Embed security in design, development, testing, release and operation, not only at the end.
4044.principle_hinglish: Security har stage me, sirf end me nahi.

4045.principle: Qualified humans must review and own AI-drafted advice.
4045.principle_hinglish: AI draft ko qualified insaan review karke own kare.

4046.principle: Match oversight to risk: light for low impact, mandatory human decisions for high impact.
4046.principle_hinglish: Risk ke hisaab se oversight rakho.

4047.principle: Mitigate automation bias with evidence display, independent judgment requirements and audits.
4047.principle_hinglish: Over-trust (automation bias) ko evidence aur audit se kam karo.

4048.principle: Design clear escalation triggers with context handoff for unusual or sensitive cases.
4048.principle_hinglish: Escalation triggers aur context handoff define karo.

4049.principle: Keep named humans as decision-makers and record rationales and overrides.
4049.principle_hinglish: Decision insaan ka, AI sirf input.

4050.principle: Provide human review routes, explanations and audit records for people affected by AI-assisted decisions.
4050.principle_hinglish: Challenge ke liye human review route aur explanation do.

4051.principle: Make human review effective with training, checklists, source links and audits.
4051.principle_hinglish: Review ko training, checklist aur audit se strong banao.

4052.principle: Expand agent autonomy in stages, based on measured reliability.

4053.principle: Maintain an inventory with named business and technical owners and a review cadence.
4053.principle_hinglish: Har assistant ka named owner aur inventory.

4054.principle: Enable easy reporting, protect reporters, and share lessons to build a safe questioning culture.
4054.principle_hinglish: Reporting easy aur safe banao, learnings share karo.
